sentences.text: ORAL ORDER [1.0] RULE.
Learned APP waives service of rule for the respondent-State.

[2.0] The present application is filed through jail under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short "BNSS") for regular bail in connection with FIR being C.R. I Part A No.154 of 2018 registered with Bapunagar police Station, Ahmedabad for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366 and 376 of IPC read with Sections, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 of the POCSO Act.

[3.0]Learned advocate for the applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the offence and the allegation against the applicant is that he jumped the bail condition, which is imposed upon him, while allowing his bail NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/16831/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined application.
It appears he could not remain present before the Trial Court and pursuant to that he detained in judicial custody.

Thereafter, he filed Criminal Misc. Application No.5561 of 2024 before the Learned Special Judge,
which came to be rejected vide order dated 30.07.2024.

sentences.text: Considering the nature of the offence, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.

[4.0] Learned APP appearing on behalf of the respondent-State has opposed the present application and submitted applicant has misused his liberty and breach of condition of not remaining present during the trial and trial is prolonged.
Hence,he has requested to dismiss the present application for regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.
It is further submitted that if the application is allowed, stringent condition may be imposed upon the applicant.
I have heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the investigation papers.
In present case, the investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
[5.0] While granting bail, the Court has to consider the involvement of the accused in the alleged offence, the jurisdiction to grant bail has to be exercised on the basis of the well settled principles having regard to the facts and circumstances of each case and the following factors are to be taken into consideration while considering an application for bail:
(i) the nature of accusation and the severity of the punishment and the nature of the materials relied upon by the prosecution;
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/16831/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined (ii) reasonable apprehension of tampering with the witnesses and threat to the complainant or the witnesses; (iii) reasonable possibility of securing the presence of the accused at the time of trial or the likelihood of his abscondence; (iv) character behaviour and standing of the accused and the circumstances which are peculiar to the accused; (v) larger interest of the public or the State and similar other considerations are required to be considered.
Following aspects have been considered:
(1) accused is already enlarged on bail but due to absence in the trial and trial was prolonged, hence, warrant came to be issued and he was taken into judicial custody;
[7.0] This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra vs. Central Bureau of Investigation reported in [2012]1 SCC 40 as well as in the case of Gudikanti Narasimhulu And Ors vs. Public Prosecutor, High Court of Andhra Pradesh reported in (1978)1 SCC 240.
Obviously, the conclusion of trial will take time and keeping the accused behind the bars is nothing but amounts to pre-trial conviction and therefore, considering the celebrated principle of bail jurisprudence is that "bail is a rule and jail is NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/16831/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined exception" as well as the concept of personal liberty guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India, present application deserves consideration.
[8.0] In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of the allegations made against the applicant in the FIR, without discussing the evidence in detail, prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.
